scheme_name: Financial Assistance for Coaching- Haryana Labour Welfare Board
description:
The Financial Assistance for Coaching scheme is an initiative launched by the Haryana Labour Welfare Board in India.

This scheme was officially launched on 1st April 2021.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial support to the children of registered construction workers in Haryana.

The scheme aims to enhance educational opportunities for these children by enabling them to access coaching for competitive examinations.

The government has set a measurable target of providing financial assistance to at least 5,000 children annually.

This initiative is particularly focused on children preparing for examinations such as the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) and the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET).

The scheme offers financial assistance of up to INR 50,000 per child for coaching classes.

This amount is intended to cover the costs associated with coaching fees, study materials, and other related expenses.

To be eligible for this financial assistance, applicants must meet specific criteria.

The applicant must be a child of a registered construction worker in Haryana.

The age limit for applicants is set at a minimum of 14 years and a maximum of 25 years.

The family income of the construction worker should not exceed INR 3 lakh per annum.

This income limit is aimed at targeting economically weaker sections of society.

In addition, the applicant must have completed their secondary education and must have secured a minimum of 50 percent marks in their Class 10 examination.

The application process for the Financial Assistance for Coaching scheme is straightforward.

Interested applicants must fill out the application form available on the official Haryana Labour Welfare Board website.

The application form requires details such as the applicant’s name, age, educational qualifications, and the name of the coaching institution.

Applicants must also submit a copy of the construction worker’s registration certificate.

Additionally, a copy of the applicant’s educational certificates must be included.

Proof of family income should also be submitted, which can be in the form of an income certificate issued by a competent authority.

Once the application form and required documents are submitted, they are reviewed by the Haryana Labour Welfare Board.

The review process typically takes about 30 days from the date of application submission.

If the application is approved, the financial assistance is disbursed directly to the coaching institution.

The disbursement is made in one installment upon approval.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board is responsible for the implementation of this scheme.

The board operates under the Department of Labour and Employment, Government of Haryana.

For any queries or assistance, applicants can contact the Haryana Labour Welfare Board at their official contact number.

The contact number for the Haryana Labour Welfare Board is 0172-2709000.

The board also provides an email address for inquiries which is hlwb-hry@hry.nic.in.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative by the Haryana government to uplift the socio-economic status of construction workers and their families.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 10 crore for the implementation of this scheme for the fiscal year 2021-2022.

This funding is aimed at ensuring that a significant number of children can benefit from the coaching assistance.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board regularly monitors the implementation of the scheme to ensure transparency and accountability.

In addition to financial assistance for coaching, the board also runs various other welfare programs for construction workers.

These programs include health insurance, maternity benefits, and scholarships for higher education.

The Financial Assistance for Coaching scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries and their families.

Many families have reported improved educational outcomes for their children due to the support provided.

The scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the overall educational development of children from economically weaker sections.

The Haryana government emphasizes the importance of education in breaking the cycle of poverty.

By providing financial assistance for coaching, the government aims to empower the next generation of construction workers’ children.

The scheme is aligned with the national goals of improving access to quality education for all.

It reflects the commitment of the Haryana government to support the welfare of its labour force.

The Financial Assistance for Coaching scheme is a crucial step towards ensuring that children from disadvantaged backgrounds have equal opportunities.

The scheme is also a part of the larger framework of social security measures introduced by the government.

Overall, the Financial Assistance for Coaching scheme represents a significant investment in the future of Haryana’s youth.

It is a proactive measure to address educational disparities and promote social equity.

The scheme is expected to have a lasting impact on the lives of many families in Haryana.

As of October 2023, the Haryana Labour Welfare Board continues to promote this initiative actively.

The board encourages eligible families to take advantage of this financial assistance to secure a better future for their children.

The scheme is a testament to the Haryana government’s dedication to improving the lives of its citizens.

The Financial Assistance for Coaching scheme is a vital resource for families striving for educational advancement.

The government remains committed to expanding and enhancing this initiative in the coming years.

This commitment includes increasing the budget allocation to accommodate more beneficiaries.

The Haryana Labour Welfare Board is continuously working to streamline the application process for better accessibility.

The scheme is a beacon of hope for many families in the construction sector.

It emphasizes the importance of education as a tool for empowerment and social mobility.

The Haryana government is determined to ensure that no child is left behind in their educational pursuits.
